When two `--add-worker` processes start with three of four seats, both can complete this count before either new worktree has acquired its agmsg identity, so both observe `seats == 3`, pass the check, and subsequently register different workers, leaving five seats. The count and creation/registration need a repository-scoped lock or reservation so concurrent additions cannot bypass the new cap.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub> Security: Keep host Git from loading worker-writable configuration**

Condition: a lower-privileged Codex worker is seated, then the Linux orchestrator removes it normally. Enabling `extensions.worktreeConfig` activates `.git/worktrees/<seat>/config.worktree`, although that entire directory is a worker-writable sandbox root. The worker can set `core.fsmonitor` to an executable in its worktree; the pre-despawn `git status` then runs it through `herdr-agents`, which is explicitly unsandboxed on Linux. A temporary-repository reproduction showed the config ignored before this flag and a marker created after it. Avoid activating executable Git settings from worker-writable metadata.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Derive the lock path from the common Git directory**

In a main checkout created with `git init --separate-git-dir`, `is_main_checkout` succeeds because `--git-dir` and `--git-common-dir` resolve to the same external directory, but `<workdir>/.git` is a file. This redirection then fails with `Not a directory`, preventing every `--add-worker` invocation in that supported repository layout. Resolve the lock location with `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`; the existing closed-row test only exercises the ordinary in-tree `.git` layout and therefore does not cover the declared common-directory behavior.
